title: Elastic reservation surface and risk-budgeting for Dedicated capacity
creator: Claire Wong
description: Define and implement an "elastic reservation surface" for Dedicated capacity that lets tenants consume reserved capacity with an explicit risk budget. This PRD covers the product, API, console UX, metrics, and rollout/rollback strategy for a feature that enables predictable guarantees while permitting controlled, billable short-term burst usage backed by a measurable risk token bank.
problem_statement: Current reserved pools are strictly carved and either admit or deny burst traffic; customers ask for predictable guarantees but want controlled, short-term overcommit while maintaining isolation and SLOs. Without a shared, auditable risk model, ops must manually adjudicate incidents and billing disputes during bursts.
goals: Provide tenants with configurable risk budgets (tokens) tied to reserved capacity that authorize short-term bursts beyond reservation without breaking global SLOs
Expose APIs and Console controls for setting budget size, recharge rate, billing rate for token consumption, and failover behavior when budget is exhausted
Make behavior observable: per-tenant risk usage, projected exhaustion time, caused preemptions, and billing events
Enable safe default policies so small customers get value without manual tuning
non_goals: Replace committed reserved capacity contracts or change core billing models for long-term reservations
Implement complex per-request ML-driven elasticity in v1 (we will rely on heuristics and simple predictive alerts)
Provide unlimited, uncontrolled bursting or bypass account-level isolation guarantees
proposed_solution: Introduce a 'risk budget' abstraction attached to a tenant's reserved pool. Risk budget is a finite token supply that can be consumed when a tenant emits requests beyond their reservation. Tokens replenish at a configurable rate (tokens/hour). Consumption has two levers: soft-allow (admit and bill) and soft-preempt (admit but mark for low-priority eviction). A global admission controller enforces system headroom by bounding aggregate risk exposure. Product surfaces: REST API (PATCH /reserved_pools/{id}/risk_budget), Console panels (budget controls, forecast chart), telemetry (risk_budget.consume, risk_budget.replenish, risk_budget.evicted). Runtime: scheduler checks budget before admitting burst; if budget insufficient, gateway falls back per tenant policy (reject, queue, route to hosted, or use model-variant).
scope: MVP (v1): API, Console controls, scheduler enforcement, billing events, basic telemetry and alerts. Exclude complex predictive autoscaling; include a simple quota-smoothing heuristic to avoid immediate exhaustion. Post-MVP: ML predictive replenishment recommendations, cross-tenant borrowing, and token marketplace.
rollout_plan: Alpha: internal customer success + 3 opt-in customers in a single region (single AZ) — duration 4 weeks
Canary: expand to 20 customers across 2 regions, monitor headroom, latency, and eviction rates — duration 6 weeks
GA: enable self-serve in Console with documentation and pricing table
Rollback: disable risk budgets per-tenant while reverting scheduler admission logic; billing events are idempotent and reversible within the invoice grace window
acceptance_criteria: API: PATCH /reserved_pools/{id}/risk_budget accepts budget_size (tokens), replenish_rate, billing_rate_per_token, and mode (soft-allow|soft-preempt). Validation tests exist and pass
Scheduler: when tenant emits bursts and risk budget available, requests are admitted and telemetry events risk_budget.consume are emitted with token_count and preemption_flag
Isolation: global risk exposure never exceeds configured cluster_headroom parameter; tests demonstrate simulated 10x burst across 100 tenants and show no SLO breach (p90 latency < baseline + 20%)
Billing: billing events produced map to ledger entries; sample invoice shows token consumption line items and matches simulated usage
Console: tenant risk panel displays current tokens, projected exhaustion time, and a one-click 'refill' or 'reduce' control; internal user test validates UI flows
Observability: dashboards show per-tenant token burn rate, top-10 consumers, projected exhaustion alerts; alerting triggers when projected exhaustion < 1 hour
Security: no sensitive keys or tenant data is leaked in risk budget telemetry; security review sign-off obtained if needed
Docs: customer-facing docs and implementation notes created (PRD → Confluence, API examples in SDKs)
open_questions: What is the canonical unit of a token for pricing (token per second of excess capacity, token per request, or token per tokenized-unit)?
Should tokens be transferable between pools owned by the same org in v1? (recommended: no)
What is an acceptable default replenish_rate to balance value vs. risk for small customers?
How do we surface fine-grained preemption logs to customers without exposing internal scheduling heuristics?
stakeholders: Eng: Rohit Kapoor (lead), Marcus Li (scheduler), Priya Shah (billing API)
success_metrics: Adoption: 30% of Dedicated tenants opt-in within 3 months of GA
Operational: zero incidents where global SLOs were violated due to risk budget admission during canary
Revenue: token consumption contributes incremental revenue of $X/month from opt-ins in first quarter
Customer satisfaction: CS NPS for Dedicated customers using risk budgets >= baseline +5
risks_mitigation: Risk: aggregate overcommit causes headroom exhaustion and latency spikes — Mitigation: conservative cluster_headroom defaults, gradual canary, automated throttles
Risk: billing disputes over token accounting — Mitigation: idempotent ledger events, clear invoice line items, replayable event logs
Risk: customers misconfigure and exhaust budget — Mitigation: Console warnings, projected exhaustion alerts, and safe fallback to tenant policy
Risk: attackers attempt to consume other tenants' budgets — Mitigation: strict RBAC, per-tenant tokens scoped to pool ID, and monitoring for anomalous burn patterns
notes: Design note: include 'forecast ribbon' in Console showing 3-hour and 24-hour projected exhaustion bands
Implementation note: ledger events should include risk_budget.window_id so we can group consumption by burst window
Telemetry: add sample events risk_budget.consume{tenant, pool_id, tokens, mode, seq_id}
Integration: coordinate with billing team to ensure token_rate pricing is available in invoices and SDKs
